title: It didn’t sound like God at first.
paragraphs: It didn’t sound like God at first.
A boy lying in the dark, somewhere between sleep and awareness, hears his name. Not thunder. Not fire. Not a shaking mountain like Exodus describes. Just… his name.
And he does what you would have done.
Because when you don’t recognize God’s voice, you default to the voices you’ve been trained to trust.
“Here I am, for you called me.”
God was speaking clearly… but Samuel didn’t yet know Him well enough to recognize His voice.
“Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, and the word of the Lord had not yet been revealed to him.” (1 Samuel 3:7)
And this is where most people don’t realize what’s really happening.
Moments when something inside you said, “Stop.”
You thought it was just your conscience.
Because like Samuel, you didn’t yet know the Lord.
And still—you went back to sleep.
Not because Eli was perfect—he wasn’t. His own sons were corrupt, and judgment was already hanging over his house. But Eli had something Samuel didn’t yet have:
On the third interruption, something clicks.
And he tells Samuel something that changes everything:
“Go, lie down, and if He calls you, you shall say, ‘Speak, Lord, for Your servant hears.’” (1 Samuel 3:9)
Samuel goes back, lies down again.
“The Lord came and stood, calling as at other times, ‘Samuel! Samuel!’” (1 Samuel 3:10)
And this time, Samuel doesn’t run to Eli.
But when Samuel finally responded correctly.
You’re waiting for God to shout.
But He’s already been calling your name.
Through that uneasiness you can’t explain.
Through the moments when everything inside you knows you’re not where you’re supposed to be.
But you keep running to other voices.
And you wonder why it still feels unclear.
Because without surrender, even a clear voice sounds confusing.
Samuel’s story doesn’t end with a gentle message either.
God gives him a hard word—a judgment against Eli’s house.
“For the Lord disciplines the one He loves…” (Hebrews 12:6)
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because hearing God isn’t the goal.
And you already know the areas where you’ve been resisting.
That delayed obedience you’ve been dressing up as “waiting.”
But here’s the grace in this moment:
God didn’t stop calling Samuel after the first misunderstanding.
Because His desire isn’t to confuse you—it’s to reach you.
“The Lord is not slow in keeping His promise… but is patient toward you, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance.” (2 Peter 3:9)
Not that you figured it out.
But that God pursued you anyway.
And the clearest voice of God isn’t just a whisper in the night.
“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Jesus didn’t wait for you to recognize Him.
And paid for your sin in full.
Because there are only two directions from here.
You keep ignoring the voice—and your heart grows quieter, colder, harder.
Even if you don’t understand everything yet.
If you know it’s time to stop running, let it be known. Write it plainly—“Speak, Lord, I’m listening.” Not for show, but because you’re done pretending.
And don’t keep this to yourself. Someone you know is still lying in the dark, hearing something they don’t understand. You might be the Eli in their life.

Follow this path if you want more than surface-level faith—if you want to actually learn to hear, recognize, and obey God’s voice through His Word, not guesswork. There’s depth waiting, correction waiting, clarity waiting.
If you’re ready to go deeper into real discipleship, where Scripture isn’t just read but lived, step into it here:
You’ll need it again when the voice comes back.
